about: Fishing villages and towns on the Coast Lab map, with SOURCED phases and population counts for the lab's year slider (1700-2025). Written by hand from fetched pages; nothing here comes from memory.

confidenceKey.high: a museum, heritage-agency or municipal document states the year(s) for the place
confidenceKey.medium: sv.wikipedia or a tourism site states the year for the place; OR a museum/municipal source says the place took part in a named period and a museum gives that period's years
confidenceKey.low: a decade or century only, years borrowed from the regional period on a weaker statement, a reading of population numbers, or the page flags its own claim as unsourced. An entry carries its weakest dated fact.

phaseRule: At a given year the phase that covers it is shown; if several cover it, the one with the latest "from" wins. "to": null means no end year is stated (shown through 2025). A place is hidden before firstRecorded; with firstRecorded null it is drawn at every year. Years with no phase show as plain "settled" (a display default, not data).
populationRule: population[] holds COUNTED observations only. At a year the lab uses the exact count, a straight-line interpolation between two counts at most 60 years apart, or the nearest count within 15 years; otherwise the house is drawn as an outline sized by its phase ("estimated"). Counts differ in what they measure (see each row's "counts" and the entry's "parish.mapping"); series have boundary breaks, noted in the rows.

scb.what: Statistics Sweden (SCB) Folkmängd per tätort, 1960-2023, read by POST from the PxWeb API; stored in tools/data/scb-tatort-population.json

wikipedia.what: Figures as printed on sv.wikipedia (each row cites its page; "note" gives the upstream source it names: SCB småorter/islands, Folkräkningen 1900, Nordisk Familjebok, Hansson 1983)
wikipedia.licence: text CC BY-SA 4.0; the figures are facts

ddbRestricted.what: Rows tagged licence "ddb-restricted" come from Tabellverket / the Demographic Data Base (Umeå), as printed on sv.wikipedia. Their terms forbid bulk download into your own database and commercial use. Kept as a handful of individually cited figures for a non-commercial preview. parish.name: Gullholmens socken
parish.mapping: the pre-1960 rows are the parish, which also holds Härmanö; Gullholmen is its main village. Härmanö has its own entry: do not add the two

notes: A kronoholme (state-owned, free to build on) until 1999. Counts from the museum report: 24 resident strandsittare in 1610, about 39 households in 1645, 20 fishing families in the late 1600s, about 100 houses around 1800. Church: chapel parish permitted 1798, church finished autumn 1799. Municipalsamhälle 29 January 1886 (sv.wikipedia).

settlements.name: Härmanö
settlements.firstRecordedNote: Figure 5 of Bohusläns museum rapport 2012:39: Felterus's map of 1673 "visande Gullholmen och Stora och Lilla Hermanö". The earlier mentions (the saga date 1253, a royal letter of 1565, a customs officer in 1572, the 1587 toll accounts) are of Hermanösund, the sound, whose location is disputed, so they are not taken as a first record of the island.

phases.note: Feldspar quarried at Höpallen and Stenvik "under 1900-talets första hälft" (half-century only; the folder says the same).

population.counts: island residents on Härmanö (118 of them in the built-up area)
population.note: sv.wikipedia: "Av befolkningen år 2000 var det 20 som bodde på ön Gullholmen och 138 på Härmanö, varav 118 i tätbebyggelsen" (read verbatim). 138 + 20 = 158, the Gullholmen parish figure for 2000
sv.wikipedia: "2012 fanns som fastboende endast 10 personer på Gullholmen och 92 på Härmanö" (read verbatim)

parish.name: Gullholmens socken
parish.mapping: the island lies in this parish; counts are island residents. The Gullholmen parish rows (to 2000) already include Härmanö, so the two are not additive

notes: Farm settlement on the east side "åtminstone sedan 1500-talet", combined with home fishing and freight sailing; the farm Härm is the oldest (Västkuststiftelsen folder). About ten house platforms from the 1500s and 1600s excavated at Skållehus. Laga skifte 1831 divided the farms in five. Nature reserve 1967. No herring, decline or resort years are stated for Härmanö itself.
